But row logic breaks: the first item y is 741 in Draft Beer vs 773 in Spirits and Wine (32 px offset), because Beer has no sub head while its neighbours do; CIDER is an H2 sitting on the same row as the Brandy/Sparkling H3s

top_problem: The idea is written down but you cannot see it. The plum 'elevator' reads as a colonnade, organ pipes or a church steeple against a staircase, and on the phone it shrinks to a plain plum stripe. The escalonado glow is a near-copy of ref-02 panel 2's stair with none of that panel's painterly craft. So the Mexico-meets-Iowa fusion lives only in proposal.md. Worse, the art is a banner plus a side rail that never talks to the type. The boldest missing idea: make ONE unmistakable silhouette (a real prairie elevator profile against a sky cut in escalonado steps) the thing the wordmark and columns lock into, so you understand the fusion in one glance without a caption.
remove: The indigo misregistration underprint (3 px offset). You cannot see it at print or phone size, so it is accumulation, not materiality. If a second cut is needed, also drop the gallery window cut-outs: the dotted row reads as Greek-key trim and pushes the tower toward 'temple'.
fixes: Redraw the elevator as one readable prairie-elevator profile: a tall slip-form bin cluster with a taller headhouse and a clear roofline, no colonnade rhythm. Make it wider and more massive so it survives the phone crop as a building rather than a stripe. Check it with a no-caption squint test on three people.

Fix the dead space and the grid switch. Either set Cocktails as two columns inside the same three-column grid (for example names and descriptions across columns 1-2, with the art interlocking in column 3), or bring the elevator's left edge into the cocktail band. Remove the 82 px void so the Cocktails-to-lower-tier gap equals the sub-group rhythm.

Align the lower-tier rows across columns: give Draft Beer an H3 ('On Draft') or drop the Agave/By the Glass sub heads to the same level, so the first items share y 773. Demote CIDER to an H3 under Draft Beer so no H2 sits on the same row as H3s.
Separate prices from names by value, not only by hue: use the muted #5B5058 or a lighter plum at Fraunces 350. Then 'Cognac VSOP 18' reads as a price at bar distance, per brief §5.

Integrate word and image. Let the stepped glow or the horizon line carry into the text area as one structural edge (for example the H2 row or the Cocktails baseline sits on the horizon step), and cut the palette to navy, amber and one ink, merging plum and dark amber into a single accent.

lens: items and prices vs draft_doc.json; ingredient names and description completeness (public_components); menu flow
problems: Prices: all 15 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rose 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Anejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Dry Cider 8). Nothing is invented or dropped. The format is consistent: inline, no $, whole numbers, plum Fraunces set right after each name, so eye travel is short. It is still only a correct baseline. The inline price moves with every name length, so nothing lines up down the page, and the cocktail block leaves roughly 40% of the text frame empty on the right.

Flow and grouping: the lower tier's hierarchy breaks. Brandy (h3) and Sparkling (h3) are pushed to the bottom of their columns with margin-top:auto, so each sits about 120 px below its parent section. On the same baseline sits CIDER, which is an h2. Read across, the row 'Brandy / CIDER / Sparkling' looks like a fourth section of equal rank. Brandy reads as detached from SPIRITS and Sparkling as detached from WINE.

Reading path in the 3-column tier is ambiguous: it can be read by row (Spirits, Beer, Wine, then Brandy, Cider, Sparkling) or by column. The proposal states Spirits, Draft Beer + Cider, Wine, but nothing in the layout enforces that order.

Section order departs from the draft (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider) and puts Spirits second. That is defensible for a cantina (agave leads), but the category it promotes holds only two thin 'pour' lines, so the choice is not earned on the page.

Descriptions for spirits repeat the item name, which is taxonomy wording: 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Anejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour'. Wine lines are generic ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine') and beer lines have no ABV. These gaps come from the draft (Rob has been asked for spirit brand/age, wine region and beer ABV), so they are not the designer's fault. However, proposal.md contains no missing_ingredients flag listing them, and criterion 8 requires one.

Cocktail ingredients: the Manhattan correctly hides aromatic bitters (public_components aromatic-bitters:false). The garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) are not in the draft components. They are cited to phg.recipe_versions via round-17/proposal.md, so I accept them as sourced, but this proposal does not re-cite them.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned has house_recipe:false. Printing names only (no specs) complies, but that should be confirmed with Rob.

Punctuation is inconsistent: only the Margarita has an internal full stop ('lime wheel. Bright and citrus-forward') and it has no final period, while every other description is a middot list with no stop. The draft's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' tasting line is the only flavour note on the menu, so the Margarita reads in a different voice from its neighbours.

Masthead line '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' is generic brand voice and states no item fact, so it passes the tagline check. The draft section intros ('Classic and house cocktails.' etc.) are dropped. That is acceptable because they are not item content.
fixes: Keep each subsection directly under its parent: remove margin-top:auto so Brandy follows Agave and Sparkling follows By the Glass, and do not let the h2 CIDER share a baseline with the h3s Brandy and Sparkling (put Cider under Draft Beer with a clear section break, or give it its own column cell at a different y).

Make the column reading order explicit, with a numbered or ruled column sequence or column-head rules that run the full tier height, so guests read Spirits then Beer/Cider then Wine rather than across rows.

Add a missing_ingredients block to proposal.md listing, for each item, what is needed (spirit brand/age for Blanco, Anejo and Cognac; region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rose; style + ABV for all three drafts and the cider), and replace the name-repeating 'X pour' lines with a neutral placeholder such as 'Ask for today's pour' until Rob supplies the data.

Use one description convention throughout: either drop 'Bright and citrus-forward' or add the source's period to it and set it on its own tasting-note line, so no single item carries a different voice.
Re-cite the garnish sources (recipe_version_id -> garnish) in this proposal, and record Rob's sign-off that naming the brown butter-washed bourbon is allowed under house_recipe:false.

lens: ingredient/garnish/label traceability to build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions; how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png
top_problem: All the facts check out, but the copy doesn't earn much. 7 of the 14 descriptions only restate the item name or a category ('Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry sparkling cider'), and the voice changes partway through the Margarita. The menu also doesn't read as a Mexican cantina: it has a single agave cocktail, no Spanish beyond Añejo and Cantina, and it gives a Manhattan, Cognac and a Czech Pilsner the same weight as the tequila.

Spirits/beer/cider/wine descriptions and all 14 prices match phg.menu_items.menu_description / menu_price for project ddc4bb5b-70e6-4581-8aae-1b4042cd75ef (trailing periods dropped consistently)
The sub-line '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' is venue copy and states no item fact; the art has no text
problems: Criterion 12: descriptions that restate the name or category: Blanco Tequila / 'Blanco tequila pour', Añejo Tequila / 'Añejo tequila pour', Cognac VSOP / 'VSOP Cognac pour'; Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé and Dry Cider get only category wording. The copy is sourced but thin (the ABV, region, brand and pour gap is known and pending with Rob).

Criterion 12/10: the Margarita alone ends its ingredient list with a period and then adds an unpunctuated sentence fragment. The other three cocktails are bare dot-lists, so the section uses two voices.

Criterion 11 (minor): capitalisation drifts from the source. 'Brown butter-washed bourbon' vs the component 'Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon', and 'Tequila blanco' / 'Rye whiskey' are sentence-cased from title-case component names. The sentence case is applied consistently, so this is not an invented fact.

Criterion 13: for a Mexican restaurant in Iowa City, Agave has two pours and no mezcal, there are no Mexican beers, and there are no Spanish section names or serve words. Only 1 of 4 cocktails is agave-based, and the Manhattan sits next to it in Classics. Spirits comes before Draft Beer and Wine, which departs from the draft_doc section order (Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider).

Criterion 14: the Margarita description breaks after 'lime wheel.' and leaves 'Bright and citrus-forward' as a line on its own. There is a dead band of about 150 px between the last cocktail and the lower tier. Spirits carry no pour or size label, and wine has no glass/bottle label beyond the 'By the Glass' subhead. Prices sit inline at 0.7 em after the name in plum tabular figures, so no price can be read against the wrong item (gate pass).

Data note, not a menu fault: phg.menu_items holds 'Junmai Ginjo' 12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'), which is absent from draft_doc.json and from the menu. Content should confirm the item was meant to be dropped.
fixes: Put Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward' on its own line in the same register as the others, or remove it, so all four cocktails use one voice and the orphan break goes away (source phg.menu_items 14555870).

Ask Rob now for producer and region (wine), style and ABV (beer and cider), and brand and pour (spirits), and until then replace the name-echo 'pour' descriptions with a flagged missing_ingredients placeholder or an empty description rather than echoing the name.
Tell the designer to reclaim the dead band between Cocktails and the lower tier, and to add pour labels (for example '1.5 oz') and a glass label for wine once Rob supplies them.

Add venue-type wording without inventing facts: Spanish subheads/kickers such as 'Clásicos' and 'De la Casa' alongside the English, and put Agave first in the lower tier explicitly as the cantina's category, since the proposal already argues for that.
Match source capitalisation for proper component names where it matters (for example 'Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon'), or state in the proposal that sentence case is the house style.
